added_failures_note: unmeasured: the reviewed manifest names no base gate log, so the added-failure count was not taken

findings.text: follow-on: _tree_bytes reimplements tree_size_bytes (reckon/crew/dispatch_launch.py:726), which routing.py already imports and calls for the same measurement at lines 2034, 2189 and 2225; the two also disagree on symlinked content (tree_size_bytes skips symlinks, _tree_bytes counts a symlink to a file via is_file()), so one added helper duplicates an owned capability and can report a size differing from the module's own elsewhere.

follow-on: the --run confinement branch of _run_has_live_pointer (confined_to == run_id returning False) is untested — no case runs gc --run for a run that still holds a live pointer and asserts its own artifacts are still offered, so the release-door behaviour the branch exists for is unexercised.

follow-on: the queued-dispatch.lock exclusion and the ledgered-lock requirement in _stale_run_locks are unguarded — no case plants a queued-dispatch.lock or a lock whose run is not in the ledger and asserts it is withheld, so a regression that offered the queue's own lock file or an unfinished run's lock would not redden.

follow-on: the manifest's cited head-arm log is truncated — it ends at 93% after 73 dots with no pytest summary line and no EXIT= line — so the run's recorded 77-passed EXIT=0 is not backed by the log it names; the claim is nonetheless true (independent re-run green), so this is an evidence-recording defect rather than a false result.

The live-pointer re-check is applied at the offering stage and again immediately before each removal.
item_verdicts.done_when: the done-when names tests/test_gc_reaches_every_crew_store.py building a temporary crew home holding, per row set, one past-retention entry, one inside retention, and one past-retention entry whose run holds a live pointer, and asserting gc reports exactly the three past-retention entries without a live pointer and gc --apply removes exactly those. The committed test (tests/test_gc_reaches_every_crew_store.py) plants exactly that (planted_stores: pr-report-old/pr-report-fresh and the general tree gen-report-live, lock-old/lock-fresh/lock-live, ud-old/ud-fresh/ud-live), asserts report_paths == {str(raw_old)} and the single lock and single run directory, that apply removes those three while the fresh and live entries survive, plus a second case that a live run keeps its lock and directory, and a third that the real crew home is untouched. I re-ran the gate in a scratch extraction of head 932c1a7c (the new test plus the existing gc, raw-report, run-directory, removal-path and worktree-residue files): 53 passed, EXIT=0 (head-arm-recheck.log). The negative control is executed and logged (gc-store-negative-control.log, EXIT=1, 1 failed / 2 passed) and I reproduced it independently: forcing _run_has_live_pointer to return False reddens the new case on assert report_paths == {str(raw_old)} with gen-report-live reported (neg-control-recheck.log, EXIT=1).
item_verdicts.goal: §3's deliverable is that garbage_collect gains three row sets — report trees under reports/<project>/ past retention and not live, lock files whose run is ledgered and not live and past retention, and run directories with neither a ledger row nor a live pointer — each reported by default and acted on only with --apply, each re-checking for a live pointer immediately before acting, every removal printing its path and size, and the existing plan-review sweep folded into the report row set. At head 932c1a7c reckon/crew/routing.py adds _run_report_trees, _stale_run_locks and _unledgered_run_directories, folds _plan_review_raw_reports into report_trees behind a family discriminator, re-reads _live_run_ids() immediately before each report.unlink/lock.unlink/shutil.rmtree, and emits path and size on every row; garbage_collect returns report_trees, lock_files and unledgered_run_directories with their *_removed counts. All three row sets and the fold are delivered.
item_verdicts.manifest: read as delivered; status complete; it names the head and negative-control logs, the three-case new test and the existing regression set, and reports a 77-passed EXIT=0 head gate; it records no baseline_suite/after_suite arm, so read_review's added-failure derivation returns unmeasured rather than zero; it records the TMPDIR collision of tests/test_gc_sweeps_orphan_scratch.py under retry_failures as environmental. Its cited head-arm log gc-store-head-arm.log is truncated — it ends at 93% after 73 dots with no pytest summary line and no EXIT= line — so the recorded 77-passed result is not backed by the log the manifest names, though my independent re-run confirms the gate green.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the section declares reckon/crew/routing.py and tests/test_gc_reaches_every_crew_store.py, and the node adds its own evidence fragment; the single commit 932c1a7c touches docs/evidence/fragments/the-crew-home-has-a-bound/gc-reaches-every-crew-store.html (+28), reckon/crew/routing.py (+273/-3) and tests/test_gc_reaches_every_crew_store.py (+283), all inside the declared paths; the declared docs/figures path is unused, which the fragment's prose carries without a figure.

justifications.durability: the central guard is independent of the fixture values — each row set is asserted to report exactly its one past-retention entry and to remove exactly those under apply, and the live run's own lock and directory are asserted to survive — and its negative control fires; but several branches ship untested: the --run confinement path in _run_has_live_pointer (routing.py:1465), the queued-dispatch.lock exclusion (routing.py:1571), a report tree whose run is neither live nor ledgered, and a lock whose run is not in the ledger, so the withdrawal rules those branches encode are unexercised.
justifications.evidence: the gate is measured and I reproduced it green (53 passed, EXIT=0, head-arm-recheck.log) and the negative control is executed and I reproduced its red (EXIT=1, neg-control-recheck.log), so the guard is shown to fire rather than merely to pass; but the run's own cited head-arm log is truncated at 93% with no summary or EXIT line, so its recorded 77-passed EXIT=0 cannot be reconciled with the artifact it names.
justifications.fit: the change reuses the module's row-dict and local-import idioms, adds no plan- or version-labelled name, and reads its new helpers in the style of the surrounding sweep; the one placement concern is that plan-review rows gain family/tree/size keys so _plan_review_raw_reports becomes a projection of report_trees, a schema change to a row set other readers may key on.
justifications.goal_fidelity: all three row sets, the --apply-only action, the pre-removal live re-check, the path-and-size report and the fold of the plan-review sweep are delivered at head 932c1a7c; the only deviation from §3's wording is that the plan-review rows now live inside report_trees behind a family discriminator while §3 asks only that the sweep be folded and not kept beside the report set.
justifications.reuse: _tree_bytes (routing.py:1443) reimplements tree_size_bytes, which this same module already imports and calls for the same measurement at routing.py:2034, 2189 and 2225, and the two diverge on symlinks (tree_size_bytes skips them, _tree_bytes counts a symlink-to-file through is_file()), so the added definition forks an owned capability rather than extending it; the remaining additions do build on the module's existing row shape.
justifications.scope_discipline: the commit touches exactly routing.py, the new test and the node's evidence fragment, all within the declared paths, and carries nothing the goal does not imply; the declared docs/figures path is left unused rather than filled with a figure the change does not need.
